entry.hops: The SSE response is a scripted writer: every write the real session frame stream makes is recorded whole, in order (the wire text); the decoder parses the data events from those writes.
entry.notRun: no HTTP server; the stream's interval timer is the mocked one
entry.runs: createSessionFrameStream (attachSse, broadcast, drain handling) with a scripted SSE response (EventEmitter; the first write returns true, later ones false when more than one string has been written), the snapshot delta encoder/decoder

normalised.reason: per-run temp path (or generated name) replaced by a placeholder

product.tree: product tree loaded by the recorder

replay.compare: mixdog-app-server thread feed (SSE frame stream under backlog): replay attach, the two session-state broadcasts and the drain; compare the writes in order, whole, and that each data event decodes to the recorded snapshot
replay.entry: A built mixdogd over its real WebSocket listener, two desktop protocol clients (packages/protocol-client connect, sessionReducer, sessionStateOf) on one thread: benchmarks/rust-core/recorders/replay-session-lane-backlog.mjs --mixdogd <exe>. Client A stops reading its socket while the opening turn (the 300 000-character row) and the live turn complete; client B, reading, must show both meanwhile; then A reads and must show each recorded publication in order. The core's slow-consumer lane is mixdog-core-base feed/mod.rs CoreFeed::publish (a full connection budget lags that connection's lane, no wait; resumed with one snapshot), covered by feed/tests.rs a_slow_consumer_lags_only_its_own_lanes.

normalised.writes: Node's SSE wire text (writeHead, ': attached', data events) is the desktop's own HTTP stream; K1's desktop takes the thread over the core's WebSocket JSON-RPC, so the user-visible content is compared through `decoded` (what the desktop decoder applied) instead
normalised.writesAfterOpen: the count of Node's SSE writes, see writes
normalised.writesAfterLive: the count of Node's SSE writes, see writes
normalised.writesTotal: the count of Node's SSE writes, see writes
normalised.maxPendingBytes: Node's SSE pending cap (8 MiB); the core bounds a connection by its event budget (CoreFeed lanes lag past it), asserted by the feed seam test
normalised.decoded[].snapshot.items[].id: the core mints its own item ids; rows are compared by text in order
normalised.promptRows: the core writes rows only through turns, so each recorded row is the answer of a turn with prompt `open`/`live`; the prompt rows and turn markers are not compared

replay.targetsCheckedAgainst: o1 6bf0a5bbf: each rust target exists at path:line, is declared `pub` and is reachable through `pub mod` or `pub use` from its crate root
